title.raw: 卷142 志一百十七 刑法一

sentences.zh: 志一百十七

translations.literal: Treatise 117
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 117

sentences.zh: 刑法一

translations.literal: Penal Law, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Penal Law, Part One

sentences.zh: 中國自書契以來，以禮教治天下。

translations.literal: Since China entered the age of written contracts, the realm has been governed through ritual teaching.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of written contracts onward, China has governed the realm through ritual and moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 勞之來之而政出焉，匡之直之而刑生焉。

translations.literal: By laboring for the people and drawing them in, government emerges; by correcting and straightening them, punishments arise.
translations.idiomatic: By nurturing and summoning the people, government takes shape; by guiding and rectifying them, penal law comes into being.

sentences.zh: 政也，刑也，凡皆以維持禮教於勿替。

translations.literal: Government and punishments alike all serve to uphold ritual teaching without decline.
translations.idiomatic: Both government and penal law exist solely to preserve ritual teaching undiminished.

sentences.zh: 故尚書曰：「明於五刑，以弼五教。

translations.literal: Therefore the Book of Documents says: 'When clearly versed in the five punishments, one assists the five teachings.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Book of Documents states: 'Be clear in the five punishments, to support the five teachings.'

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「士制百姓於刑之中，以教祗德。

translations.literal: ' Again it says: 'The scholar-official regulates the common people within the measure of punishments, thereby teaching reverent virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'The scholar-official sets the common people within the bounds of punishments, to teach reverent virtue.'

sentences.zh: 」古先哲王，其制刑之精義如此。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings fashioned punishments with such refined meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the refined meaning with which the ancient sage kings devised penal law.

sentences.zh: 周衰禮廢，典籍散失。

translations.literal: When the Zhou declined, ritual fell into ruin and the classics were scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: With the decline of the Zhou, ritual collapsed and the canonical texts were dispersed and lost.

sentences.zh: 魏李悝著法經六篇，流衍至於漢初，蕭何加為九章，歷代頗有增損分合。

translations.literal: Li Kui of Wei composed the six chapters of the Classic of Law, which spread down to the early Han, when Xiao He expanded them into nine chapters; through successive dynasties there were many additions, deletions, divisions, and mergers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui of Wei wrote the six chapters of the Classic of Law; the tradition flowed on to early Han, when Xiao He added to it to form the Nine Chapters, and successive dynasties made many additions, cuts, splits, and consolidations.

sentences.zh: 至唐永徽律出，始集其成。

translations.literal: When the Yonghui Code of the Tang appeared, the corpus was first brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the Tang Yonghui Code emerged was the body of law first gathered into a finished whole.

sentences.zh: 雖沿宋迄元、明而面目一變，然科條所布，於扶翼世教之意，未嘗不兢兢焉。

translations.literal: Although from the Song through the Yuan and Ming its outward form changed entirely, yet in the statutes promulgated the intent to support and sustain worldly teaching was never absent from earnest care.
translations.idiomatic: Though from Song through Yuan and Ming its face changed altogether, the articles issued never ceased to show scrupulous concern for bolstering the moral teaching of the age.

sentences.zh: 君子上下數千年間，觀其教化之昏明，與夫刑罰之中不中，而盛衰治亂之故，綦可睹矣。

translations.literal: Over several thousand years, the gentleman observing whether teaching was dim or bright and whether punishments hit the mark or missed it may plainly see the causes of rise and fall, order and chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Across several millennia, a thoughtful observer can plainly read the reasons for prosperity and decline, order and disorder, in whether moral instruction was enlightened or benighted and whether punishments were measured or excessive.

sentences.zh: 有清起自遼左，不三四十年混一區宇。

translations.literal: The Qing arose from the eastern Liao region and within scarcely three or four decades unified the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing rose from the Liao frontier; in little more than thirty or forty years they united the empire.

sentences.zh: 聖祖沖年踐阼，與天下休養，六十餘稔，寬恤之詔，歲不絕書。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor took the throne in his youth and gave the realm repose; for more than sixty years edicts of leniency and relief were issued without cease year after year.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacred Ancestor came to the throne as a youth and rested the realm; for more than sixty years, edicts of clemency and relief never ceased from the annals.

sentences.zh: 高宗運際昌明，一代法制，多所裁定。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor's fortune met a brilliant age, and many rulings were made upon the legal institutions of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Under the High Ancestor, when the age was flourishing, much of the dynasty's legal order was definitively settled.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以降，事多因循，未遑改作。

translations.literal: From the Renzong reign onward affairs were mostly carried on by precedent, with no leisure to undertake revision.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Renzong onward, affairs were largely left to precedent, and there was no opportunity for systematic reform.

sentences.zh: 綜其終始，列朝刑政，雖不盡清明，然如明代之廠衛、廷杖，專意戮辱士大夫，無有也。

translations.literal: Taking the dynasty as a whole, penal administration of successive reigns was not wholly lucid, yet nothing like the Ming practice of the Brocade Guard and court beating, deliberately humiliating and killing scholar-officials, ever existed.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from beginning to end, penal policy under successive reigns was not wholly clear, yet nothing comparable to the Ming's Brocade Guard and court bastinado, aimed solely at shaming and destroying the gentry, ever appeared.

sentences.zh: 治獄者雖不盡仁恕，然如漢、唐之張湯、趙禹、周興、來俊臣輩，深文慘刻，無有也。

translations.literal: Those who handled cases were not wholly humane, yet nothing like the Han and Tang figures Zhang Tang, Zhao Yu, Zhou Xing, and Lai Junchen, who twisted the law with cruel severity, ever existed.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial officers were not always merciful, yet nothing like the Han and Tang exemplars Zhang Tang, Zhao Yu, Zhou Xing, and Lai Junchen—who deepened the letter of the law with pitiless harshness—ever arose.

sentences.zh: 德宗末葉，庚子拳匪之變，創巨痛深，朝野上下，爭言變法，於是新律萌芽。

translations.literal: In the late Dezong reign the Boxer uprising of the gengzi year brought wounds vast and pain deep; court and country alike clamored for reform, and thus the new penal code began to sprout.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Guangxu reign, the Boxer catastrophe of 1900 inflicted wounds vast and pain profound; above and below the court all pressed for reform, and the new penal code began to germinate.

sentences.zh: 迨宣統遜位，而中國數千年相傳之刑典俱廢。

translations.literal: When Xuantong abdicated, the penal codes handed down through thousands of years in China were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Xuantong abdicated, China's penal codes, transmitted across millennia, had all been cast aside.

sentences.zh: 是故論有清一代之刑法，亦古今絕續之交也。

translations.literal: Therefore to discuss the penal law of the Qing as a whole is also to stand at the juncture where ancient and modern legal tradition breaks off.
translations.idiomatic: Thus to treat Qing penal law as a whole is also to stand at the break between antiquity and the present in legal tradition.

sentences.zh: 爰備志之，俾後有考焉。

translations.literal: Here it is set down in full so that posterity may have material for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is recorded here in detail, that later ages may have grounds for study.

sentences.zh: 清太祖嗣服之初，始定國政，禁悖亂，戢盜賊，法制以立。

translations.literal: At the beginning when the Qing Taizu succeeded to rule, he first fixed state policy, forbade rebellion and disorder, curbed bandits and thieves, and thereby established the legal order.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing Taizu first assumed rule, he established state policy, forbade sedition, suppressed brigandage, and thereby laid the foundations of law.

sentences.zh: 太宗繼武，於天聰七年，遣國舅阿什達爾漢等往外籓蒙古諸國宣布欽定法令，時所謂「盛京定例」是也。

translations.literal: Taizong continued the martial enterprise; in the seventh year of Tiancong he sent the imperial maternal uncle Ashdahan and others to the outer Mongol states to proclaim the imperially fixed statutes—the so-called 'Statutes Fixed at Shengjing.'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong carried on the military founding; in Tiancong 7 he sent the imperial uncle Ashdahan and others to the outer Mongol domains to proclaim the imperially ratified statutes—the so-called 'Statutes Fixed at Shengjing.'

sentences.zh: 嗣復陸續著有治罪條文，然皆因時立制，不盡垂諸久遠。

translations.literal: Thereafter articles on punishment were composed in succession, yet all were measures for the moment and were not wholly handed down for long endurance.
translations.idiomatic: Later, provisions on punishment were drafted one after another, but all were expedients for the time and were not fully intended to endure.

sentences.zh: 世祖順治元年，攝政睿親王入關定亂，六月，即令問刑衙門准依明律治罪。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shizu, the Regent Prince Rui entered the passes to settle disorder; in the sixth month he at once ordered the judicial yamen to punish crimes according to the Ming code.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1, the Regent Prince Dorgon entered the passes to quell disorder; in the sixth month he immediately ordered the judicial offices to punish offenses according to the Ming code.

sentences.zh: 八月，刑科給事中孫襄陳刑法四事，一曰定刑書：「刑之有律，猶物之有規矩準繩也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the supervising secretary Sun Xiang of the Penal Section submitted four matters on penal law; the first was fixing the penal code: 'Punishments have laws as things have compass and square.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, supervising secretary Sun Xiang of the Penal Section memorialized on four points of penal law; the first was to fix the code of punishments: 'For punishments to have laws is like things to have compass and square.'

sentences.zh: 今法司所遵及故明律令，科條繁簡，情法輕重，當稽往憲，合時宜，斟酌損益，刊定成書，布告中外，俾知畫一遵守，庶奸慝不形，風俗移易。

translations.literal: 'The laws now followed by the judicial offices and the Ming statutes and ordinances of old vary in the complexity of articles and in whether circumstances and law are light or heavy; past statutes should be examined, present needs weighed, additions and deletions made, a finished book published and proclaimed within and without, so that all may know the single standard to observe—then villainy will not take shape and customs will change.'
translations.idiomatic: 'What the judicial offices now follow, together with the old Ming statutes, differ in the density of articles and in how circumstance and penalty weigh light or heavy; past codes should be consulted, present needs weighed, additions and subtractions made, a definitive text published and proclaimed at home and abroad, so that all may know one uniform rule to obey—then wickedness will not show itself and customs will shift.'

sentences.zh: 」疏上，攝政王諭令法司會同廷臣詳繹明律，參酌時宜，集議允當，以便裁定成書，頒行天下。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, the regent ordered the judicial offices together with court ministers to expound the Ming code in detail, consult the needs of the time, deliberate until agreement, and promptly settle a finished book to promulgate throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the regent ordered the judicial offices together with court ministers to expound the Ming code in detail, consult present needs, confer until agreement, and promptly complete a definitive text for promulgation throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 十月，世祖入京，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Shizu entered the capital and assumed the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Shizu entered the capital and took the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 刑部左侍郎黨崇雅奏，在外官吏，乘茲新制未定，不無憑臆舞文之弊。

translations.literal: The left vice minister of the Ministry of Punishment Dang Chongya memorialized that local officials, while the new system was not yet fixed, were not without the abuse of twisting the text according to whim.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice minister of Punishments Dang Chongya memorialized that local officials, while the new order was unsettled, were not free of twisting the law to suit whim.

sentences.zh: 並乞暫用明律，候國制畫一，永垂令甲。

translations.literal: He also begged temporarily to use the Ming code until the national system was unified and might forever serve as binding ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the Ming code be used provisionally until the national code was unified and could serve as permanent statute.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「在外仍照明律行，如有恣意輕重等弊，指參重處。

translations.literal: The decree read: 'Outside the capital still follow the Ming code in action; if there are abuses such as arbitrary lightness or heaviness, report and punish severely.'
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read: 'Outside the capital, continue to apply the Ming code; if there are abuses such as arbitrary lightness or severity, report them for heavy punishment.'

sentences.zh: 」二年，命修律官參稽滿、漢條例，分輕重等差，從刑科都給事中李士焜請也。

translations.literal: In the second year he ordered revisers of the code to collate Manchu and Han regulations, distinguishing grades of lightness and heaviness, at the request of the chief supervising secretary of the Penal Section Li Shikun.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he ordered code revisers to collate Manchu and Han regulations, distinguishing grades of severity, at the request of chief supervising secretary of the Penal Section Li Shikun.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，大清律成，世祖御制序文曰：「朕惟太祖、太宗創業東方，民淳法簡，大辟之外，惟有鞭笞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year the Great Qing Code was completed; Shizu composed a preface saying: 'We consider that Taizu and Taizong founded the enterprise in the east; the people were simple and the law sparse—apart from capital offenses there was only the whip and the cudgel.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 3 the Great Qing Code was completed; Shizu wrote a preface stating: 'We reflect that Taizu and Taizong founded the enterprise in the east; the people were plain and the law spare—beyond capital crimes there were only flogging and beating.'

sentences.zh: 朕仰荷天休，撫臨中夏，人民既眾，情偽多端。

translations.literal: 'We have received Heaven's favor and rule the central realm; the people are numerous and truth and falsehood are manifold.'
translations.idiomatic: 'We have received Heaven's grace and rule the central realm; the people are many and truth and artifice manifold.'

sentences.zh: 每遇奏讞，輕重出入，頗煩擬議。

translations.literal: 'Whenever cases for judgment are submitted, lightness and heaviness vary widely and deliberation is quite troublesome.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Whenever cases come for judgment, lightness and severity diverge widely and deliberation is often vexing.'

sentences.zh: 律例未定，有司無所稟承。

translations.literal: 'With statutes and ordinances unsettled, the officials have nothing to which they may appeal.'
translations.idiomatic: 'With statutes unsettled, the officials have no authority to which they may appeal.'

sentences.zh: 爰敕法司官廣集廷議，詳譯明律，參以國制，增損劑量，期於平允。

translations.literal: 'Therefore We have charged the judicial officers broadly to gather court deliberation, expound the Ming code in detail, consult the national system, add and subtract and measure, with the term set on fairness.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Therefore We have charged judicial officers broadly to gather court deliberation, expound the Ming code in detail, consult our national institutions, add, subtract, and balance, aiming at fairness.'

sentences.zh: 書成奏進，朕再三覆閱，仍命內院諸臣校訂妥確，乃允刊布，名曰大清律集解附例。

translations.literal: 'When the book was completed and submitted, We reviewed it again and again, still ordered inner-court ministers to collate it until secure, and then permitted publication under the title Collected Exegesis of the Great Qing Code with Appended Precedents.'
translations.idiomatic: 'When the book was completed and presented, We reviewed it repeatedly, still ordered inner-court ministers to collate it until sound, then permitted publication under the title Collected Exegesis of the Great Qing Code with Appended Precedents.'

sentences.zh: 爾內外有司官吏，敬此成憲，勿得任意低昂，務使百官萬民，畏名義而重犯法，冀幾刑措之風，以昭我祖宗好生之德。

translations.literal: 'You officials within and without, revere this established statute; do not arbitrarily raise or lower penalties, so that officials high and low and the myriad people may fear reputation and honor the law, hoping thereby for the wind of punishments set aside, to display our ancestors' virtue of cherishing life. Descendants and subjects, guard it age after age.'
translations.idiomatic: 'You officials within and without, revere this established code; do not arbitrarily raise or lower penalties, so that officials and the myriad people may fear good name and respect the law, hoping thereby for the age when punishments lie unused, to display our ancestors' virtue of cherishing life. Descendants and subjects, guard it generation after generation.'

sentences.zh: 子孫臣民，其世世守之。

translations.literal: Descendants and subjects, guard it age after age.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants and subjects, guard it generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 」十三年，復頒滿文大清律。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Great Qing Code in Manchu was again promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 the Great Qing Code in Manchu was again promulgated.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，聖祖命大學士管理刑部尚書事對喀納等將律文復行校正。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor ordered the grand secretary managing the Ministry of Punishments Duokena and others to correct the text of the code once more.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 the Sacred Ancestor ordered grand secretary Duokena, who was managing the Ministry of Punishments, and others again to correct the text of the code.

sentences.zh: 十八年，特諭刑部定律之外，所有條例，應去應存，著九卿、詹事、科道會同詳加酌定，確議具奏。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he specially decreed that apart from the code itself, all supplementary articles should be retained or removed as appropriate, and ordered the Nine Ministers, Academicians, and Censorate jointly to deliberate in detail and report definitively.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he specially decreed that beyond the code itself, all supplementary articles should be kept or struck as appropriate, and ordered the Nine Ministers, Academicians, and Censorate jointly to deliberate in detail and report definitively.

sentences.zh: 嗣經九卿等遵旨會同更改條例，別自為書，名為現行則例。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Nine Ministers and others, obeying the decree, jointly revised the supplementary articles, which were set apart as a separate book called the Current Precedents in Force.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Nine Ministers and others, obeying the decree, jointly revised the supplementary articles into a separate book called the Current Precedents in Force.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，台臣盛符升以律例須歸一貫，乞重加考定，以垂法守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the censor Sheng Fusheng, because statutes and precedents must form one consistent body, begged renewed examination and fixing so that the law might be handed down for observance.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 censor Sheng Fusheng, holding that statutes and precedents must form one consistent body, begged renewed examination and fixing so that the law might be handed down for observance.

sentences.zh: 特交九卿議，准將現行則例附入大清律條。

translations.literal: It was specially referred to the Nine Ministers for deliberation; approval was given to attach the Current Precedents in Force to the articles of the Great Qing Code.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was specially referred to the Nine Ministers; they approved attaching the Current Precedents in Force to the articles of the Great Qing Code.

sentences.zh: 隨命大學士圖納、張玉書等為總裁。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries Tuna and Zhang Yushu and others were at once appointed general revisers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries Tuna, Zhang Yushu, and others were at once appointed chief revisers.

sentences.zh: 諸臣以律文昉自唐律，辭簡義賅，易致舛訛，於每篇正文後增用總注，疏解律義。

translations.literal: The ministers, because the text of the code derived from the Tang code and its language was concise while its meaning was compressed, easily leading to error, added general notes after the main text of each section to explicate the meaning of the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers noted that the code text derived from the Tang code—concise in wording, compressed in meaning—and easily led to error; therefore after the main text of each section they added general notes explicating the statutes.

sentences.zh: 次第酌定名例四十六條，三十四年，先行繕呈。

translations.literal: The General Principles in forty-six articles were settled in sequence; in the thirty-fourth year they were first copied and presented.
translations.idiomatic: The General Principles in forty-six articles were settled in sequence; in year 34 they were first copied and presented.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，發回刑部，命將奏聞後更改之處補入。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year they were sent back to the Ministry of Punishments with orders to insert the changes reported after submission.
translations.idiomatic: In year 36 they were returned to the Ministry of Punishments with orders to insert the changes reported after submission.

sentences.zh: 至四十六年六月，輯進四十二本，留覽未發。

translations.literal: By the sixth month of the forty-sixth year forty-two volumes were compiled and presented, retained for imperial perusal and not yet issued.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth month of year 46, forty-two volumes were compiled and presented, retained for imperial perusal and not yet issued.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，巡視東城御史湯之旭奏：「律例最關緊要，今六部見行則例，或有從重改輕，從輕擬重，有先行而今停，事同而法異者，未經畫一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, censor Tang Zhixu, touring the eastern city, memorialized: 'Statutes and precedents are of the utmost importance; the currently enforced precedents of the Six Ministries sometimes shift severity from heavy to light or from light to heavy, or what was first in force is now suspended, or the affair is the same while the law differs—none has been unified.'
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1, censor Tang Zhixu memorialized: 'Statutes and precedents are of the utmost importance; the currently enforced precedents of the Six Ministries sometimes change severity from heavy to light or light to heavy, or what was once in force is now suspended, or the case is the same while the law differs—none has been unified.'

sentences.zh: 乞簡諳練律例大臣，專掌律例館總裁，將康熙六十一年以前之例並大清會典，逐條互訂，庶免參差。

translations.literal: 'We beg that a minister well versed in statutes and precedents be selected to head the Code and Precedent Office as general reviser, and that precedents before the sixty-first year of Kangxi together with the Great Qing Institutes be collated article by article, so that discrepancies may be avoided.'
translations.idiomatic: 'We beg that a minister well versed in statutes and precedents be appointed to head the Code and Precedent Office as chief reviser, and that precedents before Kangxi 61 together with the Great Qing Institutes be collated article by article, so that discrepancies may be avoided.'

sentences.zh: 」世宗允之，命大學士硃軾等為總裁，諭令於應增應減之處，再行詳加分晰，作速修完。

translations.literal: The Shizong approved it and ordered the grand secretary Zhu Shi and others as general revisers, instructing them at points requiring addition or reduction to analyze in detail again and complete the revision swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong approved and appointed grand secretary Zhu Shi and others as chief revisers, instructing them wherever addition or reduction was needed to analyze in detail again and complete the work swiftly.

sentences.zh: 三年書成，五年頒布。

translations.literal: The book was completed in the third year and promulgated in the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: The book was completed in year 3 and promulgated in year 5.

sentences.zh: 蓋明律以名例居首，其次則分隸於六部，合計三十門，都凡四百六十條。

translations.literal: The Ming code placed the General Principles first; next it divided sub-statutes under the Six Ministries, totaling thirty sections and four hundred sixty articles in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming code placed General Principles first; next it divided sub-statutes under the Six Ministries—thirty sections in all, four hundred sixty articles.

sentences.zh: 順治初，釐定律書，將公式門之信牌移入職制，漏泄軍情移入軍政，於公式門刪漏用鈔印，於倉庫門刪鈔法，於詐偽門刪偽造寶鈔。

translations.literal: In early Shunzhi, when the code was revised, the section on credentials in the Formulas chapter was moved into Official Institutions, leaking military intelligence into Military Administration; from the Formulas chapter the improper use of paper notes was deleted, from the Granaries chapter paper currency law was deleted, from the Fraud chapter counterfeit treasure notes were deleted.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shunzhi, when the code was revised, the credentials section of Formulas was moved into Official Institutions, leaking military intelligence into Military Administration; from Formulas the improper use of paper notes was deleted, from Granaries paper currency law, from Fraud counterfeit treasure notes.

sentences.zh: 後又於名例增入邊遠充軍一條。

translations.literal: Later one article on exile to remote frontiers was added to the General Principles.
translations.idiomatic: Later one article on exile to remote frontiers was added to General Principles.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年之律，其刪除者：名例律之吏卒犯死罪、殺害軍人、在京犯罪軍民共三條，職制門選用軍職、官吏給由二條，婚姻門之蒙古、色目人婚姻一條，宮衛門之懸帶關防牌面一條。

translations.literal: In the code of Yongzheng 3, what was deleted: from General Principles, clerks and runners committing capital crimes, killing military personnel, and crimes by military and civilians in the capital—three articles; from Official Institutions, selecting military offices and officials issuing credentials—two articles; from Marriage, Mongol and semu marriages—one article; from Palace Guard, hanging pass tablets bearing seals—one article.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng 3 code, deletions included: from General Principles, clerks and runners committing capital crimes, killing military personnel, and military and civilian crimes in the capital—three articles; from Official Institutions, selecting military offices and officials issuing credentials—two; from Marriage, Mongol and semu marriages—one; from Palace Guard, hanging pass tablets bearing seals—one.

sentences.zh: 其併入者：名例之邊遠充軍並於充軍地方，公式門之毀棄制書印信並二條為一，課程門之鹽法並十二條為一，宮衛門之衝突儀仗並三條為一，郵驛門之遞送公文並三條為一。

translations.literal: What was merged: from General Principles, remote exile merged into the section on places of exile; from Formulas, destroying imperial documents and seals merged two articles into one; from Revenue Duties, salt law merged twelve articles into one; from Palace Guard, rushing imperial escorts merged three into one; from Postal Stations, forwarding official documents merged three into one.
translations.idiomatic: Merged: from General Principles, remote exile into places of exile; from Formulas, destroying imperial documents and seals—two into one; from Revenue Duties, salt law—twelve into one; from Palace Guard, rushing imperial escorts—three into one; from Postal Stations, forwarding documents—three into one.

sentences.zh: 其改易者：名例之軍官軍人免發遣更為犯罪免發遣，軍官有犯更為軍籍有犯；

translations.literal: What was altered: in General Principles, military officers and soldiers exempt from exile became criminals exempt from exile, and military officers who commit offenses became offenses by those on the military register;
translations.idiomatic: Altered: in General Principles, 'military officers and soldiers exempt from exile' became 'criminals exempt from exile,' and 'military officers who commit offenses' became 'offenses by those on the military register';

sentences.zh: 儀制門之收藏禁書及私習天文生節為收藏禁書。

translations.literal: in Rites, the sections on collecting forbidden books and privately studying astronomy were condensed into collecting forbidden books.
translations.idiomatic: in Rites, sections on collecting forbidden books and privately studying astronomy were condensed into collecting forbidden books.

sentences.zh: 其增入者：名例之天文生有犯充軍地方二條。

translations.literal: What was added: in General Principles, two articles on astronomers who commit offenses and places of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Added: in General Principles, two articles on astronomers who offend and places of exile.

sentences.zh: 總計名例律四十六條。

translations.literal: In all, the General Principles contain forty-six articles.
translations.idiomatic: In all, General Principles contain forty-six articles.

sentences.zh: 吏律：曰職制十四條，曰公式十四條。

translations.literal: Officials Code: Official Institutions fourteen articles, Formulas fourteen articles.
translations.idiomatic: Officials Code: Official Institutions fourteen articles, Formulas fourteen articles.

sentences.zh: 戶律：曰戶役十五條，曰田宅十一條，曰婚姻十七條，曰倉庫二十三條，曰課程八條，曰市廛五條。

translations.literal: Household Code: Household Service fifteen articles, Fields and Dwellings eleven, Marriage seventeen, Granaries twenty-three, Revenue Duties eight, Markets five.
translations.idiomatic: Household Code: Household Service fifteen, Fields and Dwellings eleven, Marriage seventeen, Granaries twenty-three, Revenue Duties eight, Markets five.

sentences.zh: 禮律：曰祭祀六條，曰儀制二十條。

translations.literal: Rites Code: Sacrifices six articles, Ceremonial Regulations twenty articles.
translations.idiomatic: Rites Code: Sacrifices six, Ceremonial Regulations twenty.

sentences.zh: 兵律：曰宮衛十六條，曰軍政二十一條，曰關津七條，曰廄牧十一條，曰郵驛十六條。

translations.literal: Military Code: Palace Guard sixteen, Military Administration twenty-one, Passes and Barriers seven, Stables and Herds eleven, Postal Stations sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Military Code: Palace Guard sixteen, Military Administration twenty-one, Passes and Barriers seven, Stables and Herds eleven, Postal Stations sixteen.

sentences.zh: 刑律：曰賊盜二十八條，曰人命二十條，曰鬥毆二十二條，曰罵詈八條，曰訴訟十二條，曰受贓十一條，曰詐偽十一條，曰犯奸十條，曰雜犯十一條，曰捕亡八條，曰斷獄二十九條。

translations.literal: Penal Code: Robbery and Theft twenty-eight, Homicide twenty, Assault and Battery twenty-two, Abuse eight, Litigation twelve, Accepting Bribes eleven, Fraud eleven, Adultery ten, Miscellaneous Offenses eleven, Apprehension of Fugitives eight, Trial and Sentencing twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Penal Code: Robbery and Theft twenty-eight, Homicide twenty, Assault and Battery twenty-two, Abuse eight, Litigation twelve, Accepting Bribes eleven, Fraud eleven, Adultery ten, Miscellaneous Offenses eleven, Apprehension of Fugitives eight, Trial and Sentencing twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 工律：曰營造九條，曰河防四條。

translations.literal: Works Code: Construction nine articles, River Control four articles.
translations.idiomatic: Works Code: Construction nine, River Control four.

sentences.zh: 蓋仍明律三十門，而總為四百三十六條。

translations.literal: It still followed the Ming code's thirty sections, but totaled four hundred thirty-six articles.
translations.idiomatic: It still followed the Ming code's thirty sections, but totaled four hundred thirty-six articles.

sentences.zh: 律首六贓圖、五刑圖、獄具圖、喪服圖，大都沿明之舊。

translations.literal: At the head of the code, the six diagrams of bribery grades, five punishments, instruments of punishment, and mourning garments largely followed Ming practice.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of the code, the six diagrams of bribery grades, five punishments, instruments of punishment, and mourning garments largely followed Ming practice.

sentences.zh: 納贖諸例圖、徒限內老疾收贖圖、誣輕為重收贖圖，銀數皆從現制。

translations.literal: Diagrams for commutation by payment, commutation for the aged and infirm within penal servitude limits, and commutation when a light offense was falsely charged as heavy—all silver amounts followed current regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Diagrams for commutation by payment, for the aged and infirm within penal servitude limits, and for falsely charging a light offense as heavy—all silver amounts followed current regulations.

sentences.zh: 其律文及律注，頗有增損改易。

translations.literal: The text of the code and its annotations had many additions, deletions, and alterations.
translations.idiomatic: The code text and its annotations had many additions, deletions, and alterations.

sentences.zh: 律後總注，則康熙年間所創造。

translations.literal: The general notes after the code were a creation of the Kangxi period.
translations.idiomatic: The general notes after the code were a Kangxi-era innovation.

sentences.zh: 律末並附比引律三十條。

translations.literal: At the end of the code thirty articles of analogous citation were also appended.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the code, thirty articles of analogous citation were also appended.

sentences.zh: 此其大較也。

translations.literal: Such was the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general outline.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，雖屢經纂修，然僅續增附律之條例，而律文未之或改。

translations.literal: From that time onward, although compilation and revision occurred repeatedly, only supplementary precedent articles were added; the text of the code itself was never altered.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on, although compilation and revision occurred repeatedly, only supplementary precedent articles were added; the code text itself was never changed.

sentences.zh: 惟乾隆五年，館修奏准芟除總注，並補入過失殺傷收贖一圖而已。

translations.literal: Only in the fifth year of Qianlong did the revising office memorialize approval to cut the general notes and add one diagram on commutation for negligent killing and wounding—that alone.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Qianlong 5 did the revising office memorialize approval to remove the general notes and add one diagram on commutation for negligent killing and wounding—that alone.

sentences.zh: 例文自康熙初年僅存三百二十一條，末年增一百一十五條。

translations.literal: Precedent texts from the early Kangxi period retained only three hundred twenty-one articles; by the late Kangxi period one hundred fifteen were added.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent texts from early Kangxi retained only 321 articles; by late Kangxi, 115 were added.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，分別訂定，曰原例，累朝舊例凡三百二十一條；

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 3 they were separately fixed and designated: Original Precedents, accumulated old precedents of successive reigns, three hundred twenty-one articles in all;
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 3 they were separately fixed: Original Precedents, accumulated old precedents of successive reigns—321 articles in all;

sentences.zh: 曰增例，康熙間現行例凡二百九十條；

translations.literal: Added Precedents, current precedents of the Kangxi period, two hundred ninety articles in all;
translations.idiomatic: Added Precedents, current precedents of the Kangxi period—290 articles in all;

sentences.zh: 曰欽定例，上諭及臣工條奏凡二百有四條，總計八百十有五條。

translations.literal: Imperially Fixed Precedents, imperial edicts and ministerial memorials, two hundred four articles, totaling eight hundred fifteen articles.
translations.idiomatic: Imperially Fixed Precedents, imperial edicts and ministerial memorials—204 articles; 815 in all.

sentences.zh: 其立法之善者，如犯罪存留養親，推及孀婦獨子；

translations.literal: Among well-crafted legislation: such as allowing those who commit crimes to remain to support parents, extended to widows with only sons;
translations.idiomatic: Among sound legislation: such as allowing those who commit crimes to remain to support parents, extended to widows with only sons;

sentences.zh: 若毆兄致死，並得准其承祀，恤孤嫠且教孝也。

translations.literal: if one beat an elder brother to death, permission was still granted to carry on the sacrifices—cherishing orphans and widows while teaching filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: if one beat an elder brother to death, permission was still granted to carry on the sacrifices—cherishing orphans and widows while teaching filial piety.

sentences.zh: 犯死罪非常赦所不原，察有祖父子孫陣亡，准其優免一次，勸忠也。

translations.literal: For capital crimes not normally pardoned, if investigation showed that grandfather, father, or son had died in battle array, one favorable exemption was granted—encouraging loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: For capital crimes not normally pardoned, if investigation showed grandfather, father, or son had died in battle array, one favorable exemption was granted—encouraging loyalty.

sentences.zh: 枉法贓有祿人八十兩，無祿人及不枉法贓有祿人一百二十兩，俱實絞，嚴貪墨之誅也。

translations.literal: For bent-law bribes, salaried officials at eighty taels, unsalaried officials and non-bent-law bribes for salaried officials at one hundred twenty taels—all truly strangled, strictly punishing corruption.
translations.idiomatic: For bent-law bribes, salaried officials at 80 taels; unsalaried officials and non-bent-law bribes for salaried officials at 120 taels—all truly strangled, strictly punishing corruption.

sentences.zh: 衙蠹索詐，驗贓加等治罪，懲胥役所以保良懦也。

translations.literal: Yamen parasites extorting by fraud, verified bribes punished by added grades—punishing clerks and runners to protect the weak.
translations.idiomatic: Yamen parasites extorting by fraud, verified bribes punished by added grades—punishing clerks to protect the weak.

sentences.zh: 強盜分別法無可貸、情有可原，殲渠魁、赦脅從之義也。

translations.literal: For robbery, distinguishing where the law allows no pardon and where circumstance permits mercy—exterminating ringleaders while pardoning the coerced.
translations.idiomatic: For robbery, distinguishing where the law allows no pardon and where circumstance permits mercy—exterminating ringleaders while pardoning the coerced.

sentences.zh: 復仇以國法得伸與否為斷，杜兇殘之路也。

translations.literal: Vengeance was decided by whether national law could be fulfilled or not—blocking the path of savage cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Vengeance was decided by whether national law could be fulfilled—blocking the path of savage cruelty.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸端，或隱合古義，或矯正前失，皆良法也。

translations.literal: In all these points, some tacitly accorded with ancient meaning, some corrected prior errors—all were good law.
translations.idiomatic: In all these points, some tacitly accorded with ancient meaning, some corrected prior errors—all sound law.

sentences.zh: 而要皆定制於康、雍時。

translations.literal: Yet all were customarily fixed in the Kangxi and Yongzheng periods.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all were customarily fixed in the Kangxi and Yongzheng periods.

sentences.zh: 又國初以來，凡纂修律例，類必欽命二三大臣為總裁，特開專館。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the founding of the state, whenever statutes and precedents were compiled and revised, two or three great ministers were invariably appointed as general revisers and a special office opened.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from the founding of the state, whenever statutes and precedents were compiled, two or three great ministers were invariably appointed chief revisers and a special office opened.

sentences.zh: 維時各部院則例陸續成書，苟與刑律相涉，館員俱一一釐正，故鮮乖牾。

translations.literal: At that time as the various ministries' precedents were completed one after another, if they touched penal law the office members all corrected them one by one, so that few contradictions arose.
translations.idiomatic: As the various ministries' precedents were completed, if they touched penal law the office members corrected them one by one, so few contradictions arose.

sentences.zh: 自乾隆元年，刑部奏准三年修例一次。

translations.literal: From the first year of Qianlong, the Ministry of Punishments memorialized approval to revise precedents once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: From Qianlong 1, the Ministry of Punishments memorialized approval to revise precedents once every three years.

sentences.zh: 十一年，內閣等衙門議改五年一修。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the inner court and other yamens deliberated changing this to revision once every five years.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 the inner court and other yamens deliberated changing this to revision once every five years.

sentences.zh: 由是刑部專司其事，不復簡派總裁，律例館亦遂附屬於刑曹，與他部往往不相關會。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Ministry of Punishments alone handled the matter, no longer appointing general revisers; the Code and Precedent Office was also attached to the penal ministry, often without consultation with other ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Ministry of Punishments alone handled the matter, no longer appointing chief revisers; the Code and Precedent Office was also attached to the penal ministry, often without consultation with other ministries.

sentences.zh: 高宗臨御六十年，性矜明察，每閱讞牘，必求其情罪曲當，以萬變不齊之情，欲御以萬變不齊之例。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor reigned sixty years; by nature he was strict and keenly observant; whenever he reviewed case records he invariably sought whether circumstance and guilt were properly matched, wishing to govern the endlessly varied circumstances of cases with endlessly varied precedents.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor reigned sixty years; by nature he was strict and keenly observant; whenever he reviewed case records he sought whether circumstance and guilt were properly matched, wishing to govern endlessly varied circumstances with endlessly varied precedents.

sentences.zh: 故乾隆一朝纂修八九次，刪原例、增例諸名目，而改變舊例及因案增設者為獨多。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Qianlong reign compilation and revision occurred eight or nine times; the designations Original Precedents and Added Precedents were deleted, while changes to old precedents and additions set up because of cases were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Hence under Qianlong compilation and revision occurred eight or nine times; labels such as Original and Added Precedents were dropped, while changes to old precedents and case-driven additions were especially numerous.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶以降，按期開館，沿道光、咸豐以迄同治，而條例乃增至一千八百九十有二。

translations.literal: From the Jiaqing reign onward offices opened on schedule; continuing through Daoguang, Xianfeng, and on to Tongzhi, precedents increased to one thousand eight hundred ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiaqing onward offices opened on schedule; through Daoguang, Xianfeng, and Tongzhi, precedents rose to 1,892.

sentences.zh: 蓋清代定例，一如宋時之編敕，有例不用律，律既多成虛文，而例遂愈滋繁碎。

translations.literal: In general Qing fixed precedents were like the Song compilation of edicts—when a precedent existed the code was not used; as the code largely became empty text, precedents grew ever more fragmented.
translations.idiomatic: Qing fixed precedents resembled the Song practice of compiling edicts—precedents displaced the code; as the code largely became dead letter, precedents grew ever more fragmented.

sentences.zh: 其間前後牴觸，或律外加重，或因例破律，或一事設一例，或一省一地方專一例，甚且因此例而生彼例，不惟與他部則例參差，即一例分載各門者，亦不無歧異。

translations.literal: In the interval there were contradictions before and after, or aggravation beyond the code, or breaking the code because of a precedent, or one affair one precedent, or one province or locality its own precedent—even one precedent generating another; not only did they differ from other ministries' precedents, but even one precedent split across sections was not without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile contradictions arose back and forth, penalties beyond the code, precedents overriding the code, one affair one precedent, one province or locality its own precedent—even one precedent spawning another; they diverged from other ministries' rules, and even one precedent split across sections could disagree.

sentences.zh: 展轉糾紛，易滋高下。

translations.literal: As disputes multiplied, it was easy for severity to vary high and low.
translations.idiomatic: As disputes multiplied, severity easily varied.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，世宗遺詔有曰：「國家刑罰禁令之設，所以詰奸除暴，懲貪黜邪，以端風俗，以肅官方者也。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, the Shizong's testamentary edict said: 'The establishment of the state's penal prohibitions and bans is to check villainy, remove violence, punish greed, and expel evil, to rectify custom and to make officials solemn.'
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 13, the Shizong's testamentary edict stated: 'The state's penal prohibitions and bans exist to check villainy, remove violence, punish greed, and expel evil, to rectify custom and make officials solemn.'

sentences.zh: 然寬嚴之用，又必因乎其時。

translations.literal: Yet the use of leniency and severity must also follow the times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the use of leniency and severity must also follow the times.

sentences.zh: 從前朕見人情淺薄，官吏營私，相習成風，罔知省改，不得不懲治整理，以戒將來。

translations.literal: Formerly when We saw human hearts shallow and officials pursuing private gain as a habit ingrained, ignorant of reform, We had no choice but to punish and rectify to warn the future.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, seeing shallow hearts and officials pursuing private gain as ingrained habit, ignorant of reform, We had no choice but to punish and rectify to warn the future.

sentences.zh: 今人心共知警惕矣，凡各衙門條例，有前嚴而改寬者，此乃從前部臣定議未協，朕與廷臣悉心酌核而後更定，自可垂諸永久。

translations.literal: Now all hearts together know caution; wherever precedents of each yamen were strict before and changed to lenient, this was because former ministry deliberation was not harmonious and We with court ministers deliberated carefully before changing—this may be handed down permanently.
translations.idiomatic: Now all hearts know caution; wherever yamen precedents were strict before and changed to lenient, this was because former ministry deliberation was not harmonious and We with court ministers deliberated carefully before changing—this may endure permanently.

sentences.zh: 若前寬而改嚴者，此乃整飭人心風俗之計，原欲暫行於一時，俟諸弊革除，仍可酌復舊章，此朕本意也。

translations.literal: Where they were lenient before and changed to strict, this was a plan to rectify human hearts and custom, originally intended to run only for a time; when abuses were removed the old statutes could still be weighed for restoration—this was Our original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Where they were lenient before and changed to strict, this was to rectify hearts and custom, originally intended only for a time; when abuses were removed the old statutes could still be restored—this was Our original intent.

sentences.zh: 向後遇事斟酌，如有應從舊例者，仍照舊例行。

translations.literal: Hereafter when affairs are weighed, if the old precedent should be followed, still act according to the old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter when affairs are weighed, if the old precedent should apply, still follow the old precedent.

sentences.zh: 」惜後世議法諸臣，未盡明世輕世重之故，每屆修例，第將歷奉諭旨及議准臣工條奏節次編入，從未統合全書，逐條釐正。

translations.literal: ' Alas later generations of legislators did not fully understand the reason for severity in one age and leniency in another; each time precedents were revised they only compiled imperial edicts and approved ministerial memorials in sequence, never unifying the whole book and correcting article by article.
translations.idiomatic: Alas later legislators did not fully understand severity in one age and leniency in another; each revision only compiled edicts and memorials in sequence, never unifying the whole book and correcting article by article.

sentences.zh: 穆宗號稱中興，母后柄政，削平發、捻、回疆之亂，百端待理，尚於同治九年纂修一次。

translations.literal: The Muzong reign was called restoration; the empress dowager held power; the rebellions of the Taiping, Nian, and border regions were suppressed; a hundred matters awaited order—yet in the ninth year of Tongzhi compilation was undertaken once.
translations.idiomatic: The Muzong reign was called restoration; the empress dowager held power; the Taiping, Nian, and border rebellions were suppressed; a hundred matters awaited order—yet in Tongzhi 9 compilation was undertaken once.

sentences.zh: 德宗幼沖繼統，未遑興作。

translations.literal: The Dezong succeeded young and had no leisure for new work.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong succeeded as a youth and had no leisure for new work.

sentences.zh: 兼之時勢多故，章程叢積，刑部既憚其繁猥，不敢議修，群臣亦未有言及者，因循久之。

translations.literal: Moreover the times were troubled and regulations piled up; the Ministry of Punishments feared the mass and dared not propose revision; no minister spoke of it either—procrastination lasted long.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover times were troubled and regulations piled up; the Ministry of Punishments feared the mass and dared not propose revision; no minister spoke of it—procrastination lasted long.

sentences.zh: 逮光緒二十六年，聯軍入京，兩宮西狩。

translations.literal: By the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu the allied armies entered the capital and the two palaces fled west.
translations.idiomatic: By Guangxu 26 the allied armies entered the capital and the two palaces fled west.

sentences.zh: 憂時之士，咸謂非取法歐、美，不足以圖強。

translations.literal: Men anxious for the times all said that without taking Europe and America as model strength could not be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Men anxious for the times all said that without taking Europe and America as model, strength could not be attained.

sentences.zh: 於是條陳時事者，頗稍稍議及刑律。

translations.literal: Thus those who memorialized on current affairs began little by little to discuss penal law.
translations.idiomatic: Thus memorialists on current affairs began little by little to discuss penal law.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，直隸總督袁世凱、兩江總督劉坤一、湖廣總督張之洞，會保刑部左侍郎沈家本、出使美國大臣伍廷芳修訂法律，兼取中西。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Zhili governor-general Yuan Shikai, the Liangjiang governor-general Liu Kunyi, and the Huguang governor-general Zhang Zhidong jointly recommended the left vice minister of Punishments Shen Jiaben and the minister plenipotentiary to the United States Wu Tingfang to revise the laws, drawing on both China and the West.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28, Zhili governor-general Yuan Shikai, Liangjiang governor-general Liu Kunyi, and Huguang governor-general Zhang Zhidong jointly recommended left vice minister of Punishments Shen Jiaben and minister plenipotentiary to the United States Wu Tingfang to revise the laws, drawing on China and the West.

sentences.zh: 旨如所請，並諭將一切現行律例，按照通商交涉情形，參酌各國法律，妥為擬議，務期中外通行，有裨治理。

translations.literal: The decree approved as requested and also instructed that all current statutes and precedents be drafted with reference to treaty and commercial circumstances, consulting the laws of various countries, so that Chinese and foreigners might both follow them and governance be aided.
translations.idiomatic: The decree approved as requested and instructed that all current statutes and precedents be drafted with reference to treaty and commercial circumstances, consulting foreign laws, so that Chinese and foreigners might both follow them and governance be aided.

sentences.zh: 自此而議律者，乃群措意於領事裁判權。

translations.literal: From this those who deliberated on law turned their minds in a body to consular jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: From this, those who deliberated on law turned their minds to consular jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 是年刑部亦奏請開館修例。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Punishments also memorialized to open an office to revise precedents.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Punishments also memorialized to open an office to revise precedents.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，先將例內今昔情形不同，及例文無關引用，或兩例重複，或舊例停止者，奏准刪除三百四十四條。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, precedents whose present circumstances differed from the past, or whose text was irrelevant to citation, or duplicated another precedent, or old precedents suspended, were first memorialized for deletion—three hundred forty-four articles.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31, precedents whose circumstances differed from the past, or were irrelevant, or duplicated, or were suspended, were first memorialized for deletion—344 articles.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，更命侍郎俞廉三與沈家本俱充修訂法律大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year the vice minister Yu Liansan was also ordered to serve with Shen Jiaben as revising law ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 33, vice minister Yu Liansan was also ordered to serve with Shen Jiaben as revising law ministers.

sentences.zh: 沈家本等乃徵集館員，分科纂輯，並延聘東西各國之博士律師，藉備顧問。

translations.literal: Shen Jiaben and others then gathered office members to compile by section and also engaged doctors of law from East and West as consultants.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiaben and others gathered office members to compile by section and engaged East and West doctors of law as consultants.

sentences.zh: 其前數年編纂未竣之舊律，亦特設編案處，歸併分修。

translations.literal: The old code not yet finished in compilation in prior years also had a special drafting office set up for consolidated division of labor.
translations.idiomatic: The old code not yet finished in prior years also had a special drafting office for consolidated division of labor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遵旨議定滿、漢通行刑律，又刪並舊例四十九條。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, obeying the decree, the Manchu and Han universally applied penal code was deliberated and fixed, and forty-nine old precedents were again deleted and merged.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, obeying the decree, the universally applied Manchu and Han penal code was deliberated and fixed, and 49 old precedents were again deleted and merged.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，全書纂成繕進，諭交憲政編查館核議。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong the whole book was compiled and submitted; it was ordered referred to the Constitutional Compilation and Investigation Office for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 the whole book was compiled and submitted; it was ordered referred to the Constitutional Compilation Office for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 二年，覆奏訂定，名為現行刑律。

translations.literal: In the second year it was reported back as fixed, named the Current Penal Code.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 it was reported back as fixed, named the Current Penal Code.

sentences.zh: 時官制改變，立憲詔下，東西洋學說朋興。

translations.literal: At that time the official system changed, the constitutional edict was issued, and Eastern and Western learning flourished together.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the official system changed, the constitutional edict was issued, and Eastern and Western learning flourished.

sentences.zh: 律雖仍舊分三十門，而芟削六部之目。

translations.literal: Although the code still followed the old thirty sections, the headings of the Six Ministries were cut away.
translations.idiomatic: Although the code still followed the old thirty sections, the Six Ministries headings were removed.

sentences.zh: 其因時事推移及新章遞嬗而刪者，如名例之犯罪免發遣、軍籍有犯、流囚家屬、流犯在道會赦、天文生有犯、工樂戶及婦人犯罪、充軍地方，職制之大臣專擅選官、文官不許封公侯、官員赴任過限、無故不朝參公座、奸黨，公式之照刷文卷、磨勘卷宗、封掌印信，戶役之丁夫差遣不平、隱蔽差役、逃避差役，田宅之任所置買田宅，婚姻之同姓為婚、良賤為婚姻，課程之監臨勢要中鹽、阻壞鹽法、私礬、舶商匿貨，禮制之朝見留難，宮衛之內府工作人匠替役，軍政之邊境申索軍需、公侯私役官軍、夜禁，關津之私越冒度關津、詐冒給路引、遞送逃軍妻女出城、私出外境及違禁下海、私役弓兵，廄牧之公使人等索借馬匹，郵驛之占宿驛舍上房，賊盜之起除刺字，鬥毆之良賤相毆，訴訟之軍民約會、詞訟誣告、充軍及遷徙，受贓之私受公侯財物，犯奸之良賤相奸，雜犯之搬做雜劇，捕亡之徒流人逃，斷獄之徒囚不應役，營造之有司官吏不住公廨是也。

translations.literal: What was deleted as times shifted and new regulations succeeded included: from General Principles, criminals exempt from exile, offenses on the military register, families of exiles, exiles meeting amnesty on the road, astronomers who offend, artisans and musicians and women who commit crimes, places of exile; from Official Institutions, great ministers monopolizing selection of officials, civil officials not permitted to enfeoff as duke or marquis, officials exceeding limits in proceeding to post, absenting themselves without cause from joint audience at the public seat, factions; from Formulas, brushing document copies, grinding and examining dossiers, sealing and keeping seals; from Household Service, unfair dispatch of corvée labor, concealing corvée labor, evading corvée labor; from Fields and Dwellings, purchasing fields and dwellings at one's post; from Marriage, marriage within the same surname, marriage between free and debased status; from Revenue Duties, powerful persons mediating in salt, obstructing salt law, private alum, merchant ships concealing goods; from Ceremonial Regulations, detaining those who come to court audience; from Palace Guard, artisans of the inner palace substituting for corvée; from Military Administration, demanding military supplies at the border, dukes and marquis privately employing official troops, night curfew; from Passes and Barriers, privately crossing or falsely crossing passes, falsely obtaining travel permits, forwarding escaped soldiers' wives and daughters out of the city, privately going beyond the border and forbidden going to sea, privately employing archers; from Stables and Herds, public messengers and the like demanding to borrow horses; from Postal Stations, occupying upper rooms at relay stations; from Robbery and Theft, removing tattoo marks; from Assault and Battery, free persons and debased persons beating each other; from Litigation, military and civilians making appointments, false accusation in lawsuits, exile and relocation; from Accepting Bribes, privately receiving goods from dukes and marquis; from Adultery, free persons and debased persons committing adultery with each other; from Miscellaneous Offenses, performing miscellaneous plays; from Apprehension of Fugitives, escaped penal laborers; from Trial and Sentencing, prisoners who should not labor; from Construction, responsible officials not residing in the public yamen—that is the tally.
translations.idiomatic: Deleted as times shifted included: from General Principles, criminals exempt from exile, military register offenses, families of exiles, exiles meeting amnesty on the road, offending astronomers, artisans and musicians and women offenders, places of exile; from Official Institutions, ministers monopolizing selection, civil officials enfeoffing as duke or marquis, exceeding post limits, absenting joint audience, factions; from Formulas, brushing copies, examining dossiers, sealing seals; from Household Service, unfair corvée dispatch, concealing corvée, evading corvée; from Fields and Dwellings, purchasing property at one's post; from Marriage, same-surname marriage, free-debased marriage; from Revenue Duties, powerful salt mediation, obstructing salt law, private alum, concealing merchant goods; from Ceremonial Regulations, detaining court audience; from Palace Guard, inner-palace artisan substitution; from Military Administration, border military demands, dukes employing troops, night curfew; from Passes and Barriers, illegal crossing, false permits, forwarding escaped soldiers' families, forbidden sea travel, private archers; from Stables and Herds, demanding horses; from Postal Stations, occupying relay upper rooms; from Robbery and Theft, removing tattoo marks; from Assault, free-debased mutual beating; from Litigation, military-civilian appointments, false accusation, exile; from Bribes, receiving from dukes; from Adultery, free-debased adultery; from Miscellaneous, performing plays; from Apprehension, escaped laborers; from Trial, prisoners not laboring; from Construction, officials not residing in public yamen—and so on.

sentences.zh: 其緣政體及刑制遷變而改者，如名例之化外人有犯改為蒙古及入國籍人有犯，徒流遷徙地方改為五徒三流二遣地方，婚姻之娶樂人為妻妾改娶娼妓為妻，人命之殺子孫及奴婢圖賴人節去「及奴婢」字，鬥毆之奴婢毆家長改為僱工人毆家長，罵詈之奴婢罵家長改為僱工人罵家長，犯奸之奴婢奸家長妻改為僱工人奸家長妻是也。

translations.literal: What was altered because political form and penal system shifted included: from General Principles, foreigners who commit offenses changed to Mongols and persons who acquire nationality who commit offenses, places for penal servitude exile and relocation changed to places for the five penal servitudes three exiles and two banishments; from Marriage, taking musicians as wives and concubines changed to taking prostitutes as wives; from Homicide, the section on killing children and grandchildren and slaves and servants to frame others—the words 'and slaves and servants' were cut; from Assault and Battery, slaves and servants beating the master of the house changed to hired workers beating the master of the house; from Abuse, slaves and servants cursing the master changed to hired workers cursing the master; from Adultery, slaves and servants committing adultery with the master's wife changed to hired workers committing adultery with the master's wife—that is the tally.
translations.idiomatic: Altered as polity and penal system shifted: from General Principles, 'foreigners who offend' became 'Mongols and persons who acquire nationality who offend,' exile places became places for five penal servitudes, three exiles, and two banishments; from Marriage, taking musicians as wives became taking prostitutes as wives; from Homicide, killing children and slaves to frame others—'and slaves' was cut; from Assault, slaves beating masters became hired workers beating masters; from Abuse, slaves cursing masters became hired workers cursing masters; from Adultery, slaves with master's wife became hired workers with master's wife—and so on.

sentences.zh: 綜計全律仍存三百八十有九條，而比引律則刪存及半，依類散入各門，不列比附之目。

translations.literal: In all the whole code still retained three hundred eighty-nine articles, while analogous citation statutes were deleted to half remaining, distributed by category into each section without listing a section of analogy.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the whole code retained 389 articles; analogous citation statutes were cut to half, distributed by category without a separate analogy section.

sentences.zh: 舊例除刪並外，合續纂之新例，統一千六十六條。

translations.literal: Apart from deletions and mergers, together with newly compiled precedents, there were one thousand sixty-six in all.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from deletions and mergers, together with newly compiled precedents, there were 1,066 in all.

sentences.zh: 其督捕則例一書，順治朝命臣工纂進，原為旗下逃奴而設。

translations.literal: The book of precedents for supervising apprehension was ordered by ministers to compile and submit in the Shunzhi reign; it was originally established for escaped bondservants under the banners.
translations.idiomatic: The Supervising Apprehension Precedents were ordered compiled in Shunzhi; they were originally for escaped banner bondservants.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年重加酌定，乾隆以後續有增入，計條文一百一十，亦經分別去留，附入刑律，而全書悉廢。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi it was again weighed and fixed; after Qianlong additions continued to enter, totaling one hundred ten articles, also separately retained or removed and attached to the penal code, while the whole book was entirely abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15 it was again weighed and fixed; after Qianlong additions continued, totaling 110 articles, also separately retained or removed and attached to the penal code, while the whole book was abolished.

sentences.zh: 律首仍載服制全圖，以重禮教。

translations.literal: At the head of the code the full diagram of mourning garments was still carried, to honor ritual teaching.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of the code the full mourning-garment diagram was still carried, to honor ritual teaching.

sentences.zh: 是年冬頒行焉。

translations.literal: It was promulgated that winter.
translations.idiomatic: It was promulgated that winter.

sentences.zh: 若蒙古治罪各條，載諸理籓院則例，及西寧番子治罪條例，別行諸岷、洮等處者，以其習俗既殊，刑制亦異，未敢輕議更張。

translations.literal: As for the various articles on punishing Mongols, carried in the Institutes of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and the regulations for punishing Xining Tibetans, separately enforced in Min and Tao and other places—because their customs were already different and penal systems also differed, no light change was ventured.
translations.idiomatic: Articles on punishing Mongols in the Court of Colonial Affairs Institutes, and Xining Tibetan punishment regulations enforced separately in Min, Tao, and elsewhere—because customs and penal systems differed, no light change was ventured.

sentences.zh: 新律則光緒三十二年法律館撰上刑民訴訟律，酌取英、美陪審制度。

translations.literal: The new code: in the thirty-second year of Guangxu the Law Office drafted and submitted criminal and civil procedure laws, drawing on the British and American jury system.
translations.idiomatic: The new code: in Guangxu 32 the Law Office drafted criminal and civil procedure laws, drawing on British and American jury systems.

sentences.zh: 各督撫多議其窒礙，遂寢。

translations.literal: Most governor-generals deliberated that it was obstructive and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Most governor-generals found it obstructive and the matter was shelved.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，復先後奏上新刑律草案，總則十七章：曰法例，曰不論罪，曰未遂罪，曰累犯罪，曰俱發罪，曰共犯罪，曰刑名，曰宥恕減輕，曰自首減免，曰酌量減輕，曰加減例，曰緩刑，曰暫釋，曰恩赦，曰時效，曰時期計算，曰文例。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year they again memorialized in succession the draft new penal code; the General Part seventeen chapters: called Legal Examples, called Crimes Not Punishable Regardless, Attempted Crimes, Accumulated Crimes, Concurrent Crimes, Joint Crimes, Names of Punishments, Pardon and Mitigation, Self-Accusation and Mitigation, Discretionary Mitigation, Examples of Increase and Decrease, Suspended Sentence, Temporary Release, Amnesty, Limitation Period, Calculation of Time Periods, Textual Examples.
translations.idiomatic: In year 33 they again memorialized the draft new penal code; General Part seventeen chapters: Legal Examples, Crimes Not Punishable Regardless, Attempted Crimes, Accumulated Crimes, Concurrent Crimes, Joint Crimes, Names of Punishments, Pardon and Mitigation, Self-Accusation and Mitigation, Discretionary Mitigation, Examples of Increase and Decrease, Suspended Sentence, Temporary Release, Amnesty, Limitation Period, Calculation of Time Periods, Textual Examples.

sentences.zh: 分則三十六章：曰關於帝室之罪，曰關於內亂之罪，曰關於國交之罪，曰關於外患之罪，曰關於漏泄機務之罪，曰關於瀆職之罪，曰關於妨害公務之罪，曰關於選舉之罪，曰關於騷擾之罪，曰關於逮捕監禁者脫逃之罪，曰關於藏匿罪人及湮滅證據之罪，曰關於偽證及誣告之罪，曰關於放火決水及水利之罪，曰關於危險物之罪，曰關於往來通信之罪，曰關於秩序之罪，曰關於偽造貨幣之罪，曰關於偽造文書及印文之罪，曰關於偽造度量衡之罪，曰關於祀典及墳墓之罪，曰關於鴉片煙之罪，曰關於賭博彩票之罪，曰關於奸非及重婚之罪，曰關於飲料水之罪，曰關於衛生之罪，曰關於殺傷之罪，曰關於墮胎之罪，曰關於遺棄之罪，曰關於逮捕監禁之罪，曰關於略誘及和誘之罪，曰關於安全信用名譽及秘密之罪，曰關於竊盜及強盜之罪，曰關於詐欺取財之罪，曰關於侵佔之罪，曰關於贓物之罪，曰關於毀棄損壞之罪。

translations.literal: Special Part thirty-six chapters: called Crimes Concerning the Imperial House, Crimes Concerning Internal Disorder, Crimes Concerning Foreign Relations, Crimes Concerning External Threat, Crimes Concerning Leaking State Secrets, Crimes Concerning Malfeasance, Crimes Concerning Obstructing Official Business, Crimes Concerning Elections, Crimes Concerning Disturbance, Crimes Concerning Escape from Arrest and Imprisonment, Crimes Concerning Concealing Criminals and Destroying Evidence, Crimes Concerning False Testimony and False Accusation, Crimes Concerning Arson, Flood, and Water Works, Crimes Concerning Dangerous Substances, Crimes Concerning Communications, Crimes Concerning Public Order, Crimes Concerning Counterfeiting Currency, Crimes Concerning Forging Documents and Seals, Crimes Concerning Forging Weights and Measures, Crimes Concerning Sacrifices and Graves, Crimes Concerning Opium, Crimes Concerning Gambling and Lotteries, Crimes Concerning Adultery and Bigamy, Crimes Concerning Drinking Water, Crimes Concerning Public Health, Crimes Concerning Killing and Wounding, Crimes Concerning Abortion, Crimes Concerning Abandonment, Crimes Concerning Arrest and Imprisonment, Crimes Concerning Abduction and Enticement, Crimes Concerning Safety, Credit, Reputation, and Secrecy, Crimes Concerning Theft and Robbery, Crimes Concerning Fraud to Obtain Property, Crimes Concerning Embezzlement, Crimes Concerning Stolen Goods, Crimes Concerning Destruction and Damage.
translations.idiomatic: Special Part thirty-six chapters: Crimes Concerning the Imperial House, Internal Disorder, Foreign Relations, External Threat, Leaking State Secrets, Malfeasance, Obstructing Official Business, Elections, Disturbance, Escape from Arrest and Imprisonment, Concealing Criminals and Destroying Evidence, False Testimony and False Accusation, Arson, Flood, and Water Works, Dangerous Substances, Communications, Public Order, Counterfeiting Currency, Forging Documents and Seals, Forging Weights and Measures, Sacrifices and Graves, Opium, Gambling and Lotteries, Adultery and Bigamy, Drinking Water, Public Health, Killing and Wounding, Abortion, Abandonment, Arrest and Imprisonment, Abduction and Enticement, Safety, Credit, Reputation, and Secrecy, Theft and Robbery, Fraud to Obtain Property, Embezzlement, Stolen Goods, Destruction and Damage.

sentences.zh: 兩編合共三百八十七條，經憲政編查館奏交部院及疆臣覈議，簽駁者夥。

translations.literal: The two parts together totaled three hundred eighty-seven articles; referred by the Constitutional Compilation Office to ministries and border officials for verification, those who annotated objections were many.
translations.idiomatic: The two parts totaled 387 articles; referred to ministries and border officials for verification, objections were many.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，沈家本等彙集各說，復奏進修正草案。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, Shen Jiaben and others gathered the various opinions and again memorialized the revised draft.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1, Shen Jiaben and others gathered opinions and again memorialized the revised draft.

sentences.zh: 時江蘇提學使勞乃宣上書憲政編查館論之曰：「法律大臣會同法部奏進修改刑律，義關倫常諸條，未依舊律修入。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiangsu provincial education commissioner Lao Nai-xuan memorialized the Constitutional Compilation Office, arguing: 'The law ministers together with the Ministry of Law memorialized the revised penal code; articles concerning human relations and constant principles were not revised into the old code as entries.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jiangsu provincial education commissioner Lao Naixuan memorialized the Constitutional Compilation Office: 'The law ministers together with the Ministry of Law memorialized the revised penal code; articles concerning human relations and constant principles were not revised into the old code.'

sentences.zh: 但於附則稱中國宗教遵孔，以綱常禮教為重。

translations.literal: 'But in the supplementary provisions it says China's religion honors Confucius and regards the constants of human relations and ritual teaching as weighty.'
translations.idiomatic: 'But the supplementary provisions say China's religion honors Confucius and regards the constants of human relations and ritual teaching as weighty.'

sentences.zh: 如律中十惡親屬容隱，干名犯義，存留養親，及親屬相奸、相盜、相毆，發冢犯奸各條，未便蔑棄。

translations.literal: 'Such as in the code the ten abominations, relatives concealing one another, offenses against the name of elders, remaining to support parents, and relatives committing adultery, theft, or beating one another, grave robbery and adultery—each article cannot lightly be cast aside.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Such as the ten abominations, relatives concealing one another, offenses against elders' names, remaining to support parents, relatives committing adultery, theft, or beating one another, grave robbery and adultery—each cannot lightly be cast aside.'

sentences.zh: 中國人有犯以上各罪，應仍依舊律，別輯單行法，以昭懲創。

translations.literal: 'When Chinese commit the above crimes they should still follow the old code; a separate single law should be compiled to display punishment and correction.'
translations.idiomatic: 'When Chinese commit the above crimes they should still follow the old code; a separate law should be compiled to display punishment.'

sentences.zh: 竊維修訂新律，本為籌備立憲，統一法權。

translations.literal: 'We consider that revising the new code was originally to prepare constitutional government and unify legal authority.'
translations.idiomatic: 'We consider that revising the new code was originally to prepare constitutional government and unify legal authority.'

sentences.zh: 凡中國人及在中國居住之外國人，皆應服從同一法律。

translations.literal: 'All Chinese and foreigners residing in China should obey the same law.'
translations.idiomatic: 'All Chinese and foreigners residing in China should obey the same law.'

sentences.zh: 是此法律，本當以治中國人為主。

translations.literal: 'This law should originally take governing Chinese as its main purpose.'
translations.idiomatic: 'This law should originally govern Chinese as its main purpose.'

sentences.zh: 今乃依舊律別輯中國人單行法，是視此新刑律專為外國人設矣。

translations.literal: 'Now to compile a separate Chinese law according to the old code is to regard this new penal code as set up solely for foreigners.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Now to compile a separate Chinese law according to the old code is to regard this new penal code as solely for foreigners.'

sentences.zh: 本末倒置，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: 'Root and branch inverted—nothing exceeds this.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Root and branch inverted—nothing exceeds this.'

sentences.zh: 草案案語謂修訂刑律，所以收回領事裁判權。

translations.literal: 'The draft's case language says revising the penal code is to recover consular jurisdiction.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The draft's case language says revising the penal code recovers consular jurisdiction.'

sentences.zh: 刑律內有一二條為外國人所不遵奉，即無收回裁判權之實。

translations.literal: 'If within the penal code one or two articles are not observed by foreigners, there is no reality of recovering jurisdiction.'
translations.idiomatic: 'If one or two articles are not observed by foreigners, there is no reality of recovering jurisdiction.'

sentences.zh: 故所修刑律，專以摹仿外國為事。

translations.literal: 'Therefore the penal code revised specializes in imitating foreign countries in all matters.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Therefore the revised penal code specializes in imitating foreign countries.'

sentences.zh: 此說實不盡然。

translations.literal: 'This statement is not wholly so.'
translations.idiomatic: 'This statement is not wholly so.'

sentences.zh: 泰西各國，凡外國人居其國中，無不服從其國法律，不得執本國無此律以相爭，亦不得恃本國有此律以相抗。

translations.literal: 'In all Western countries, whenever foreigners reside in their country they must obey that country's law; they may not argue that their own country has no such law, nor may they resist on the ground that their own country has such a law.'
translations.idiomatic: 'In all Western countries, foreigners residing there must obey that country's law; they may not argue their own country has no such law, nor resist on the ground their own country has such a law.'

sentences.zh: 今中國修訂刑律，乃謂為收回領事裁判權，必盡舍固有之禮教風俗，一一摹仿外國。

translations.literal: 'Now China revises the penal code yet says it is to recover consular jurisdiction and must wholly abandon inherent ritual teaching and custom, imitating foreign countries in every point.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Now China revises the penal code yet says it recovers consular jurisdiction and must wholly abandon inherent ritual teaching and custom, imitating foreign countries in every point.'

sentences.zh: 則同乎此國者，彼國有違言，同乎彼國者，此國又相反，是必窮之道也。

translations.literal: 'Then what agrees with this country, that country objects; what agrees with that country, this country opposes in turn—this is necessarily a dead end.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Then what agrees with this country, that country objects; what agrees with that country, this country opposes—a dead end.'

sentences.zh: 總之一國之律，必與各國之律相同，然後乃能令國內居住之外國人遵奉，萬萬無此理，亦萬萬無此事。

translations.literal: 'In sum a country's laws must be identical with every country's laws before foreigners residing within can be made to obey—by no means is there such a principle, and by no means will such a thing happen.'
translations.idiomatic: 'In sum a country's laws must be identical with every country's laws before foreigners within can obey—no such principle, and no such thing will happen.'

sentences.zh: 以此為收回領事裁判權之策，是終古無收回之望也。

translations.literal: 'To take this as the policy for recovering consular jurisdiction is to have no hope of recovery from first to last.'
translations.idiomatic: 'To take this as policy for recovering consular jurisdiction is to have no hope of recovery ever.'

sentences.zh: 且夫國之有刑，所以弼教。

translations.literal: 'Moreover a state has punishments in order to assist teaching.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Moreover a state has punishments to assist teaching.'

sentences.zh: 一國之民有不遵禮教者，以刑齊之。

translations.literal: 'When the people of a country do not observe ritual teaching, punishments align them.'
translations.idiomatic: 'When a country's people do not observe ritual teaching, punishments align them.'

sentences.zh: 所謂禮防未然，刑禁已然，相輔而行，不可缺一者也。

translations.literal: 'What is called ritual guarding the not-yet-arisen, punishments forbidding the already-arisen—mutually assisting in action, neither can be lacking.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Ritual guards what has not yet arisen, punishments forbid what has arisen—they assist each other; neither can be lacking.'

sentences.zh: 故各省簽駁草案，每以維持風化立論，而案語乃指為渾道德法律為一。

translations.literal: 'Therefore when each province annotated the draft they often argued from maintaining custom; yet the case language pointed to this as confusing morality and law into one.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Therefore provinces annotating the draft often argued from maintaining custom; yet the case language called this confusing morality and law.'

sentences.zh: 其論無夫奸曰：『國家立法，期於令行禁止。

translations.literal: 'Its argument on adultery without a husband said: "The state legislates expecting orders to be carried out and prohibitions observed.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Its argument on adultery without a husband said: "The state legislates expecting orders enforced and prohibitions observed.'

sentences.zh: 有法而不能行，轉使民玩法而肆無忌憚。

translations.literal: 'When there is law that cannot be enforced, it instead makes the people treat law as a game and act without dread.'
translations.idiomatic: 'When law cannot be enforced, it makes the people treat law as a game and act without dread.'

sentences.zh: 和姦之事，幾于禁之無可禁，誅之不勝誅，即刑章具在，亦祗具文。

translations.literal: 'Matters of consensual adultery are nearly impossible to forbid, impossible to punish in excess; even when penal articles exist they are only empty text.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Consensual adultery is nearly impossible to forbid, impossible to punish in excess; even when penal articles exist they are only empty text.'

sentences.zh: 必教育普及，家庭嚴正，輿論之力盛，廉恥之心生，然後淫靡之風可少衰。

translations.literal: 'Only when education is universal, families strict, the force of public opinion strong, and hearts of shame born can the wind of debauchery somewhat decline.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Only when education is universal, families strict, public opinion strong, and shame born can debauchery somewhat decline.'

translations.literal: '" Again it said: "To check such ugly conduct lies not in law but in teaching.'
translations.idiomatic: '" Again: "To check such conduct lies not in law but in teaching.'

sentences.zh: 即列為專條，亦無實際。

translations.literal: 'Even if listed as a special article there is no practical effect.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Even as a special article there is no practical effect.'

sentences.zh: 』其立論在離法律與道德教化而二之，視法律為全無關於道德教化，故一意摹仿外國，而於舊律義關倫常諸條棄之如遺，焉用此法為乎？

translations.literal: '" Its argument stood in separating law from moral teaching into two, viewing law as wholly unrelated to moral teaching; therefore it imitated foreign countries in one direction and cast aside like refuse old code articles concerning human relations and constants—of what use is such a law?'
translations.idiomatic: '" Its argument separated law from moral teaching, viewing law as wholly unrelated to moral teaching; therefore it imitated foreign countries and cast aside old code articles on human relations—of what use is such a law?'

sentences.zh: 」謂宜將舊律有關禮教倫紀各節，逐一修入正文，並擬補干名犯義、犯罪存留養親、親屬相奸相毆、無夫奸、子孫違犯教令各條。

translations.literal: ' It proposed that sections of the old code concerning ritual teaching and human relations be revised one by one into the main text, and also proposed supplementing offenses against elders' names, remaining to support parents, relatives committing adultery or beating one another, adultery without a husband, and children and grandchildren violating parental orders.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that old-code sections on ritual teaching and human relations be revised into the main text, and supplementing offenses against elders' names, remaining to support parents, relatives committing adultery or beating one another, adultery without a husband, and children violating parental orders.

sentences.zh: 法律館爭之。

translations.literal: The Law Office disputed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Law Office disputed this.

sentences.zh: 明年資政院開，憲政編查館奏交院議，將總則通過。

translations.literal: The next year the Consultative Assembly opened; the Constitutional Compilation Office memorialized referring it to the Assembly for deliberation, and the General Part was passed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Consultative Assembly opened; the Constitutional Compilation Office referred it to the Assembly, and the General Part passed.

sentences.zh: 時勞乃宣充議員，與同院內閣學士陳寶琛等，於無夫奸及違犯教令二條尤力持不少怠，而分則遂未議決。

translations.literal: At that time Lao Naixuan served as a member, and with fellow members such as Grand Secretariat academician Chen Baochen within the Assembly, on adultery without a husband and violating parental orders in particular they held firm without slackening, while the Special Part was therefore not deliberated to conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Naixuan served as a member; with Chen Baochen and others, on adultery without a husband and violating parental orders they held firm, while the Special Part was not deliberated to conclusion.

sentences.zh: 餘如民律、商律、刑事訴訟律、民事訴訟律、國籍法俱編纂告竣，未經核議。

translations.literal: The rest, such as civil code, commercial code, criminal procedure law, and civil procedure law and nationality law, were all compiled and finished but not verified.
translations.idiomatic: Civil code, commercial code, criminal and civil procedure laws, and nationality law were all compiled but not verified.

sentences.zh: 惟法院編制法、違警律、禁煙條例均經宣統二年頒布，與現行刑律僅行之一年，而遜位之詔下矣。

translations.literal: Only the Court Organization Law, Police Offenses Law, and Anti-Opium Regulations were all promulgated in the second year of Xuantong; together with the Current Penal Code they ran only one year before the abdication edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Court Organization Law, Police Offenses Law, and Anti-Opium Regulations were promulgated in Xuantong 2; with the Current Penal Code they ran only one year before the abdication edict.
